items.followUp: Define covalent radius and give one example.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is defined using the distance between the nuclei of two adjacent atoms.
rubric.description: Defines atomic radius as half the distance between the nuclei of two adjacent atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The question also requires an example.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of an atomic radius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable element and its radius, or a valid diatomic example.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two adjacent atoms of the same element.
For example, the atomic radius of sodium is about 186 pm.

items.followUp: Explain why oil does not dissolve readily in water.

rubric.why: The principle refers to the similar nature of solute and solvent.
rubric.description: States that substances with similar nature dissolve in one another: polar in polar and non-polar in non-polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the principle or its correct explanation.

rubric.description: Gives a suitable example, such as salt dissolving in water or iodine dissolving in a non-polar solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example or for correctly applying the principle to oil and water.

modelAnswer: The principle “like dissolves like” means polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents and non-polar solutes dissolve in non-polar solvents.
For example, sodium chloride dissolves in polar water, whereas non-polar oil does not dissolve readily in water.

items.followUp: Define molarity and write its formula.

rubric.why: These definitions specify the volume-percentage and mass-per-volume percentage measures.
rubric.description: Correctly defines V/V % and W/V % using the volume of solution as the denominator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct definitions or equivalent formulae for V/V % and W/V %.

rubric.why: W/W % is defined using masses of solute and solution.
rubric.description: Correctly defines W/W % using the mass of solution as the denominator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition or formula.

modelAnswer: V/V % = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.
W/V % = (mass of solute in g ÷ volume of solution in mL) × 100.
W/W % = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.
